Press walnut-sized pieces onto a grater to shape them like dates.
Bake in a 180 °C oven for 30 minutes.
Pour the cold syrup over the hot cookies and garnish with pistachios.
Shaping on a grater is traditional.
Bülbül yuvası (nightingale’s nests)
1 cup ground pistachios
Brush the pastry with butter, roll around a thin rolling pin and pull out while scrunching.
Curl the scrunched pastry into round nest shapes and arrange on the tray.
Put pistachios in the centres and drizzle with butter.
Pour over the cold syrup.
The centres of the nests should be filled with pistachios.
Bread kadayıf (with kaymak)
1 ready-made bread kadayıf
200 g kaymak
Put the kadayıf on a tray, pour hot water over it to soften for 5 minutes and drain.
Boil the sugar and water and add the lemon.
Pour the hot syrup over the kadayıf.
Cook over a low heat or in a 180 °C oven for 20 minutes until the syrup is absorbed.
Once cool, serve with kaymak and pistachios.
Dövme ice cream can be used instead of kaymak.
Pestil and walnut sucuk (homemade)
2 litres grape juice, or 1 litre grape molasses and 1 litre water
1 cup cornflour
2 cups walnut kernels
4 pieces of thick cotton string, 50 cm each
Thread the walnuts onto the string with a needle.
Dissolve the flour and cornflour in some of the grape juice without lumps.
Boil the rest of the grape juice, add the mixture and stir until it thickens to a paste.
Dip the walnut strings into the paste, lift out, dry for 10 minutes and repeat 3–4 times.
Dry in an airy, shady place for 1 week.
Spread the remaining paste thinly on a tray and dry to make pestil.
Drying should be done in an airy, dust-free place.
Sliced.

İnegöl köfte
500 g beef mince (low fat)
Knead the mince, squeezed onion, bicarbonate of soda, salt and black pepper for 10 minutes.
Rest in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Shape finger-thick köfte about 6 cm long.
Cook on a hot grill for 4 minutes on each side.
Serve with piyaz and roasted peppers.
No bread is added; kneading and resting give the köfte its texture.
Tekirdağ köfte
Knead all the ingredients for 10 minutes.
Leave the mixture in the fridge for 1 hour.
Shape into flat, rectangular walnut-sized köfte.
Grill for 4–5 minutes on each side.
Serve with piyaz and roasted tomatoes.
A thin, even shape ensures even cooking.
Akçaabat köfte
1 teaspoon black pepper
Soak and squeeze the bread.
Knead the mince, bread, crushed garlic and spices.
Shape into thick, oval köfte.
Cook on a grill or in a cast-iron pan for 5 minutes on each side.
Serve with roasted peppers and rice.
Garlic is the distinctive flavour of the Trabzon style.
Hasanpaşa köfte (meatballs topped with mash)
1 slice stale bread
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper
Make a köfte mixture with the mince, onion, egg, bread and spices, shape round köfte and make a hollow in the middle of each.
Boil the potatoes and make a mash with milk and butter.
Fill the hollows of the köfte with mash and arrange in a baking dish.
Thin the tomato paste with 1 cup hot water and pour it around the edges.
Sprinkle with kashar and bake in a 190 °C oven for 35 minutes.
If the mash is thick, it won’t run in the oven.
Beyti kebab
500 g minced lamb
Knead the mince with garlic, chilli flakes and salt and shape onto skewers or into long köfte.
Grill for 10 minutes, turning.
Wrap in lavash and cut into 3 cm slices.
Melt the tomato paste in butter and drizzle over the slices.
Wrapping the lavash tightly stops the slices falling apart.
Urfa kebab
600 g minced lamb (fatty)
To serve: 4 roasted tomatoes, 4 green peppers, 4 lavash, 1 onion, isot
Knead the mince with salt for 10 minutes; no chilli is added.
Press onto flat skewers.
Cook over charcoal for 8–10 minutes, turning.
Roast the tomatoes and peppers too.
Serve with lavash, sumac onions and isot.
It differs from Adana kebab in not being spicy.
Elbasan tava (lamb baked in yogurt)
500 g diced lamb
Topping: 2 cups yogurt, 2 eggs, 2 tablespoons flour
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper, 1 dessert spoon thyme
Brown the meat in butter and cook with a little water for 1 hour until tender.
Transfer the meat with its juices to a baking dish.
Whisk the yogurt, eggs, flour and salt.
Pour the mixture over the meat.
Bake in a 200 °C oven for 25 minutes until golden on top, then sprinkle with thyme.
An Ottoman dish that comes from Albanian cuisine.
Sultan kebab (pastry parcels)
4 sheets baklava pastry
Cook the meat in its own juices, then fry with onion, pepper, tomato and tomato paste.
Let the filling cool.
Divide the pastry sheets, add the filling and kashar and fold into parcels.
Brush with egg yolk.
Bake in a 200 °C oven for 25 minutes until golden.
If the filling isn’t cooled, the pastry goes soft.
Stuffed dried vegetables (aubergine and pepper)
20 dried aubergines and dried peppers
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 dessert spoon chilli flakes, 1 dessert spoon mint
Boil the dried vegetables for 5 minutes to soften them.
Knead the mince, rice, grated tomato, tomato paste, oil and spices.
Stuff the vegetables with the filling and arrange in a pot.
Place an upturned plate on top and add hot water.
Cook over a low heat for 50–60 minutes.
Made in winter in Gaziantep and Eastern cuisine.
Fresh broad beans in olive oil
1 kg fresh broad beans
Trim the tips and side strings of the pods, cut into 3 cm pieces and soak in water with lemon and flour.
Soften the onions in olive oil.
Add the beans, sugar, salt and 1 cup hot water.
Sprinkle with dill and serve cold with yogurt.
Water with flour and lemon stops the beans browning.
